    Prism — the six-hour runcurrent · R-PRG-001 R-MOT-002 R-NTF-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-085
    ★ the transcript assumes entries SETTLE. A training run takes a day.
 
docker verbs settle in seconds. An agent turn takes a minute. Neither
breaks the model. A six-hour run does, and it is Prism's own problem —
no other consumer has it.
 
three things break at once
 
  1  the entry remains unsettled for hours, so its tail is not yet final
  2  it SCROLLS AWAY. Submit a run, do twenty other things, and the
     thing you care about is 300 rows up
  3  the activity line is the AGENT'S and it SCROLLS AWAY. A run has
     a loss curve, a step count, a queue position and a node
 
and the answer is already in the design — it is the agent row
 
  » auto   ✦ qwen3-coder-next   effort high            localhost:8000   22:13
  ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  12%  6k/50k   step ░░░░░░░░░░ —   28 tok/s
  ~/code/calcium   ⎇ feat/c26   +124/-18 ~1   ✎ 3   ⋯ 2 watching   malachy
  ⋯ › a3f9b21  █████░░░░░░░ 43%  ep 17/40     f410d99  queued       ⌃⇥ switch
 
a WATCH is not a tab and not a push — it is a pointer INTO the
transcript. Selecting one scrolls to its entry and expands it.
 
  ⇧⇥       focus the watch row
  ←→       move among watches
  ⏎        scroll to its entry and open it
  watch.jump[n] remains an action and receives a direct chord only when
  the resolved profile can assign one without a collision. ⌃⇥ remains
  exclusively frame/tab switching.
  /watch   pin one that is not yours
  /unwatch or it drops itself when the run ends
 
  so the record stays whole, nothing is hidden, and the live state
  is in the one place this document already puts live state.
 
what a run's ENTRY looks like while it runs, six hours in
 
● submit digit-classifier · 6h 02m · ep 17/40
  ⎿ a3f9b21 · gpu-04 · 2×A100 · !1248
    ██████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  43%   ep 17 of 40   ~7h 48m left
    val loss  █▇▆▅▄▃▃▂▂▂▁▁  0.0372   ↓ from 0.41
    gpu       ▅▇█▇██▇██▇██  94%
    ≡ logs   ⚡ events   ⊘ cancel   ⏎ the full view
 
five rows, not a dashboard. An identity/provenance row, a progress bar,
a metric sparkline, a utilisation sparkline and a verb row — it PATCHES
in place rather than appending, so six hours of a run is still five rows.
 
  which is an ordinary patchable block doing exactly what it was built for, and
  a streaming reply is a PATCH through the transport — the same shape
  /logs takes. Any design that says stream means patch.
 
so the answer to “shell, dashboard, or both”
 
  A SHELL. The dashboard is a VERB — /dashboard emits one as an entry,
  and it settles like any other. It is a picture of a moment, not a
  place you live in.
  
  the thing people actually want from a dashboard — is my run still
  going — is the watch row, and it costs one line instead of a screen.
    

    Prism — which plots it actually needscurrent · R-PRG-001 R-COL-004 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-086
    the survey lists forty forms. A run needs FOUR; five including sweeps.
 
  a metric over steps    line          the one everybody opens
  progress               bar           block — progress · continuous · active
  a metric in a row      sparkline     inside a table cell
  runs compared          dumbbell      two points, the gap is the answer
 
  and one more the moment there is a sweep:
  is a gap real          forest        an interval and a pooled row
 
what Prism is the consumer FOR, and does not need
 
  treemap · sankey · chord · radar · waffle · icicle · gantt
  spectrogram · violin · ridgeline · contour · plot3d
  
  each has a consumer somewhere — the profiler wants six of them — but
  not here. Prism was the app the ML plot package was justified BY, so
  it is the app that gets to say which dozen, and a chart it does not
  need is a chart nobody needed.
 
  ▲ which is worth writing down rather than leaving implied: forty
  forms shipped; four per run — five including sweeps — are load-bearing
  for the consumer they were built for. That is a finding about the survey, not a complaint
  about the forms.
 
the ML blocks that ARE load-bearing, and none needs a new plot form
 
  cost         GPU-hours and money, per run and per sweep — the
               number management asks about and nobody surfaces
  lineage      which dataset produced the checkpoint this model
               was fine-tuned from. Nobody can answer it at 3am
  throughput   samples/s with an ETA, which is a progress bar
               that has learnt to divide
 
  two of the three already reduce to a progress bar and a table. They are unbuilt
  because they are unglamorous, not because they are hard.
    

    Reconciling with C16 and C26current · R-QST-001 R-COR-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-087
    C16 and C26 were written before this pass. Where they disagree with it,
here is which wins and why.
 
the specs are the authority on MECHANISM. This document is the authority
on SHAPE. A binding is a shape; the store it writes is a mechanism.
 
what changed, and every one is a binding rather than a behaviour
 
  newline          ⌥⏎  →  ⇧⏎      what people type, and the
                                   protocol makes it detectable
  copy             y     →  ⌃⇧C     a letter types a letter
  bottom           G     →  ⌘↓       it was never a mode
  find             ⌃r    →  ⌃⇧F     find, as everywhere else
  scroll           ⇞ ⇟   →  ⌥↑↓     ⇞ ⇟ are not on a laptop
  move by entry    n p   →  ↑↓       they were always arrows
  leave the prompt —     →  ⇧⇥      shift-tab moves focus back
  switch agent     —     →  ⌃⇥      agents are tabs
 
  none of these changes what the key DOES — the action, the store
  and the frame are the specs'. Only the chord moved.
 
what this pass ADDS that the specs have no row for
 
  focusGround         a lightness ground for the cursor. C10 has
                      selection and no focus surface
  keyboardProtocol    C02's tenth capability field. It is
                      UNCONSIDERED there, not deferred
  per-binding repeat  DAS and ARR as a decision, which needs the
                      protocol's release events to exist at all
  the scope footer    the last line naming the live keys
 
★ and one RULE needed refining, because the legend caught it
 
  I wrote NO SINGLE-LETTER COMMANDS ON CONTENT. But the gesture
  table has 1–9 toggling a plot's series, which is exactly that.
  
  the rule's REASON was: while an editor owns input, ordinary text keys
  keep typing there without a focus check. The rule bites wherever typing
  is possible; non-typing owners may declare single-key actions.
  
  corrected: NO SINGLE-KEY COMMANDS IN ANY SCOPE WHERE TYPING IS
  POSSIBLE. Inside a block nothing is typed, so 1–9 on a legend and
  r to reset a camera are legal and good.
  
  which is the shape of correction this whole exercise keeps
  producing: the rule was right and its statement was too wide.
 
what the specs got right and this document IMPORTED unchanged
 
  click again is a state test, not a timing one
  focus memory, resolved by id, falling forward
  hover may preview inline targets or move a plot readout; never moves focus
  or commits domain/action state
  press arms; release commits only to the same stable identity
  right-click has no key equal, so it has no effect
  a click on a non-element row is unconsumed
  a selection cannot straddle two entries
  the wheel acts on the box under the POINTER, not the focused one
 
  all eight are better than anything I would have arrived at, and
  six of them are answers to questions I had not thought to ask.
 
what to do when they conflict during the build
 
  1  a CHORD conflict — this document wins, and the spec's row is
     updated rather than exempted
  2  a MECHANISM conflict — the spec wins, and this document is
     wrong about how something works
  3  a RULE conflict — neither wins automatically. Find the rule's
     reason and check whether it reaches the case, as the legend
     did above
 
  and the third is the common one, which is why a rule in this
  document without its reason beside it is a rule that will be
  applied somewhere it does not belong.
    

    Four major things this document owedcurrent · R-MOT-001 R-PER-001 R-NTF-001 R-COL-006 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-088
    four major things this document owed, and now says
 
1 · MOTION: FULL / REDUCED / OFF — independent of colour depth
  the design is kinetic, and there was no way to turn it down. mouse: off
  already exists; motion joins it as an independent preference because
  a 1-bit display may animate and a 24-bit display may be still.
  
  ● updating the tests   12s · 1.4k tok      the mark is STILL
  ● pytest · 4.2s · 47 passed          no spinner, no ramp
  
  the elapsed counter carries liveness, which this document already
  calls the honest answer. The mark's job is one bit and a static
  mark still carries it.
 
2 · /permissions — a standing grant is a one-way door without it
   what                      where                 granted 
   edits                     ~/code/calcium        22:14   
   rg --stats -uu            the count agent       22:41   
   npm test                  ~/code/calcium        3d ago  
  ↑↓ move   ⌥⌫ revoke   ⌃⇧C copy
  
  always allow is a decision, and a decision you cannot see is one
  you cannot revoke — the same argument /config's source column makes.
 
3 · A WATCHED RUN ENDING EARNS THE BELL
  the notification ladder fires on TURN end. A six-hour run finishing
  is not a turn — and a watch drops itself when the run ends, so being
  away meant it vanished from the footer with no trace.
  
  ⟩ a question is waiting         always
  ● a WATCHED RUN ended           always — new
  ● a watched run FAILED          always — new
  ● a turn ended                 if it ran over ~30s
  ● a tool call ended            never — the turn has not
 
4 · A METRIC'S DIRECTION DRIVES ITS TREND TONE
  val loss   █▇▆▅▄▃▃▂▂▁  0.0372   ↓ from 0.41    lower is better
  accuracy   ▁▂▃▄▅▆▆▇██  0.941    ↑ from 0.62    higher is better
  val loss   ▁▂▄▅▆▇▇███  0.410   ↑ from 0.04    … and this is BAD
  
  a trend that always paints DOWN as ok misleads on half of every ML
  metric. The METRIC declares its polarity and the arrow takes ok or
  error from it — otherwise the colour is decorative, which this
  document argues against everywhere else.
 
and two smaller ones
 
  FIND says what it cannot reach: 3 of 14 · loaded turns only
  the transcript evicts at a cap, so a count over the loaded window is
  a bounded window — and a bounded window says what it dropped.
  
  A SUBAGENT'S HUE SKIPS THE PARENT'S. Hues are assigned by index, but
  a reader can pin main to any of them with /colour. The assignment
  excludes whatever main currently holds, however it got it — two
  agents in one colour is the thing the hue exists to prevent.
    

    One hierarchy, and what sits beside itcurrent · R-OWN-001 R-STA-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-089
    ONE HIERARCHY, with independent owners and target classes beside it
 
  owner route: frame / tab  →  scope  →  substate  →  focused element
  independent target: a selection range or set may overlap the focused element
 
  a FRAME     a tab. Its own prompt, context and scopes. ⌃⇥ sideways
  a SCOPE     prompt · transcript · block. Three, and they nest
  a SUBSTATE  find, completion, history search. It handles first, then passes
              to the prompt scope below it
  an ELEMENT  what has focus inside the scope
  a SELECTION what would be copied
 
  and a blocking QUESTION sits BESIDE the hierarchy and owns input while
  it is open. It is not a rung, which is why esc RESOLVES its declared
  safe path rather than leaking into the held scope.
  A captured CHILD also sits beside it: an attached PTY transfers ownership
  without becoming a substate; only host.detach returns ownership.
 
★ A QUESTION IS ONE IDENTITY WITH INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES
 
  answerForm · placement · blocking · owner · dismissal · safeResolution
  inspectionPath · editorState · residue
  
  CHOICE             normally REPLACES; ←→ and ⏎ choose an answer
  TEXT               normally FLOATS above the held prompt and uses
                     a question-scoped editor
  
  PANEL, PEEK and OVERLAY describe layer behaviour, not question type.
 
★ TWO TARGET CLASSES, which settles the click argument
 
  DIRECT-ACTION    a link, a button, a chip, a toggle, a legend entry,
                   a choice. ONE CLICK acts. There is nothing to be
                   inside, so focus-then-activate would be ceremony
  FOCUS-FIRST      a row, a plot, an expandable block, a slider. The
                   first click FOCUSES, the second ACTIVATES — because
                   entering one changes what the arrows drive
  
  the earlier text said both, in different sections, without naming
  the axis. The axis is whether the target HAS AN INSIDE.
 
★ FOCUS IS VISIBLY INTENSIFIED, by a SHAPE-SPECIFIC treatment
 
  an unpainted RUN or BOX inverts — its own tone becomes its ground
  a FRAME          its border or axes take the tone and go heavy
  a CONTROL        a wash over label, track and value
  a PAINTED IDENTITY chip bolds and takes a mark; the hue is its
                   identity and must not move
  
  the old “active means invert, everywhere” claim was true of two of the four, and
  the document drew the other two correctly while claiming otherwise.
 
★ HOVER MAY PREVIEW. It never moves focus, activates or commits domain state.
 
  a link, a button, a chip   previews its focus treatment
  a cursorable plot          moves the readout
  everything else            nothing
  
  “nothing, everywhere else” was already false in three sections. The
  rule that survives is the CONSEQUENCE, not the coverage.
 
★ IN THE ENTRY GUTTER, ● IS A WORK UNIT. The COLUMN says whose.
 
● I'll check the parser first.                  col 0 — the agent
● read_file(parse.ts) · 184 lines       col 0 — its call
  ├─ ●  count   verify the count       indented — a child's
    ● 7c2d4e1  decoder-zoom      succeeded      a table row
  
  “● is always the agent” was never true — it marks a unit of work,
  and the gutter column plus the indentation say who owns it.
 
★ PASSIVE against REJECTED, which is the honest form of the last rule
 
  PASSIVE — unconsumed, silent   an unarmed release, a right-click, a click
                                 on blank space, hover on nothing
  REJECTED — explains itself     a key with no action HERE, a
                                 disabled control, a refused paste
  
  “nothing silently does nothing” meant REJECTED. A pointer event with
  no target was never a command, and explaining it would be noise.
    

    Semantic names against visual aliasescurrent · R-COL-001 R-COL-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-090
    SEMANTIC NAMES AND VISUAL ALIASES ARE NOT THE SAME THING
 
the palette was reused for syntax, provenance and postures, and the
argument for it was good: one palette, and a reader who has learnt that
the identifier tone means A NAME learns nothing new looking at code.
 
but reuse of a HUE became reuse of a NAME, and the names make claims:
  a syntax string was ok        nothing succeeded
  a syntax number was warn      nothing is near a limit
  a config flag was error        nothing failed
  the skip posture was error     it is a mode, not a failure
 
★ so: six namespaces, and a theme may map them to the same hue
 
  status.ok  status.warn  status.error  status.info
  content.default  content.dim  content.muted  content.identifier
  interaction.focus  interaction.selection  interaction.current
  syntax.keyword  syntax.string  syntax.number  syntax.comment
  provenance.default  provenance.config  provenance.env  provenance.flag
  posture.manual  posture.acceptEdits  posture.plan  posture.auto  posture.skip
 
  syntax.string RESOLVES to the same green as status.ok in every theme
  shipped here. Nothing on screen changes. What changes is that a
  theme CAN break the mapping, and that no token any longer says
  something succeeded about a string literal.
 
  this costs nothing visually and it is the audit the 1-bit rung
  already gets: a distinction you cannot name is one you cannot check.
 
★ semantic ink and surface resolve as one composition
 
  ink(role, surface, state, theme)
  themes may define composed tokens such as status.error.on.selection,
  content.muted.on.focus and content.identifier.on.diffAdd. Inheritance
  is valid only when the resulting pair passes the contrast audit.
 
  normal text targets 4.5:1. UI boundaries, large marks and the dedicated
  interaction.focusIndicator target 3:1 against adjacent colours.
  Every supported tone × surface × theme × colour-depth pair is generated
  and tested, including high-contrast themes at their declared target.
 
★ state is a product, not a list of competing adjectives
 
  lifecycle × outcome × resolution × ownership × focus × pointer × selection × choice
  × disclosure × availability × freshness × validity. Hover and focus can coexist; pointer armed is
  not a synonym for ownership or selection.
  FOCUS IS NEVER INFERRED FROM SELECTION. A persistent focus mark or edge
  survives when selection or a semantic ground already occupies the cell.
 
  one cell still paints one ground. The composition table chooses it and
  preserves displaced facts through mark, edge, weight, underline or text.
  Required fixtures include focused+selected+failed, selection over diff,
  focus over a heatmap, disabled+error and stale+running.
 
and the tone budget is REGIONAL, not global
 
  an ordinary entry   three semantic tones. Five is a smell
  a code block        its own six-slot syntax palette
  a plot              its own series palette
  a patch             its own add/remove pair
  identity chrome     its own ten hues
  
  a full frame counting twelve tones is not breaking the rule — the
  rule was about one ENTRY, and it was stated globally.
 
status red, scoped so visual aliases do not inherit its meaning
 
  WITHIN FRAMEWORK STATUS AND OVERRIDE TOKENS, RED MEANS FAILURE OR
  UNSAFE OVERRIDE, and every use carries a TEXTUAL OR SYMBOLIC CARRIER.
  syntax, patch removal, and reader-selected identity hues are visual
  aliases. They keep their own named roles and do not inherit status meaning.
  
   ERROR         a failure       — the word
  !! skip         an unsafe mode  — the !! and the words
  flag            an override     — the column says provenance
   prod           a warning       — the reader typed it themselves
  
  “error is the only red” was false four ways. What is true is that no
  red is ever the ONLY carrier, which is the 1-bit rule doing the work
  the colour rule was claiming.
    

    State tables — seven core facts per componentcurrent · R-TAB-001 · example R-EXA-091
    seven required facts per component, all checkable; axis-specific rows may extend them.
 
  ENTRY        what puts it on screen
  CARRIERS     what says what it is — and there are always at least two
  ACTIONS      what a key or a click does to it
  ESC          where esc lands, by the published order
  MOTION OFF   its form with no animation at all
  1-BIT        its form with no colour at all
  RESIDUE      what is left once it settles
 
  prose said all of this. A table makes a missing cell VISIBLE, which is
  the failure this document keeps finding — a rule stated in one section
  and quietly unstated in the next.
 
 A CALL                                                                      
  entry        the model invokes a tool
  carriers     ● mark · verb · duration slot · result-summary slot · ⎿ gutter
  running      ● white STILL, spinner in the duration slot
  actions      ⏎ expand / enter · ⌃⇧C copies invocation AND output
  esc          out to the transcript
  motion off   the spinner is omitted; static ● plus elapsed carry liveness
  1-bit        ● still; outcome in bold; the gutter unchanged
  residue      ● ok · verb · duration · a NUMBER. Never “succeeded”
 
 A QUESTION — CHOICE                                                         
  entry        a tool, a command or the app needs an answer
  placement    declared; replace is the default · blocking yes · owner question
  carriers     ⟩ mark · focused choice painted · chosen answer keeps ✓ · safe path named
  actions      ←→ move focus · ⏎ answer · click a choice · inspect suspends
               the same unresolved question
  esc          takes the declared safe path: answer, cancel, or step back one arm
  motion off   unchanged — it never animated
  1-bit        › on the focused choice; ✓ remains on a chosen answer
  residue      question · terminal resolution · answer when one exists
 
 A QUESTION — TEXT                                                           
  entry        an answer needs a sentence, not a choice
  placement    float · blocking yes · owner question editor
  carriers     ⟩ and the question above the held prompt · shared editor code
  actions      ⏎ submits · ⇧⏎ newline · editing operations are shared;
               buffer, history and undo are question-scoped
  esc          cancels the QUESTION, not the text
  motion off   the caret stops blinking; nothing else changes
  1-bit        unchanged
  residue      question · terminal resolution · sentence when submitted
 
 A BOUNDED BLOCK                                                             
  entry        a call or a command produced more rows than fit
  carriers     the window · a RESIDUE ROW saying how many are hidden
  actions      ⏎ enters · ↑↓ rows · ⇧↑↓ selects · ⌃⇧C copies SOURCE
  esc          out to the transcript, remembering the row
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        the focused row inverts; the residue row is unchanged
  residue      the window and its count. It does not re-expand on its own
 
 A STREAMING REPLY                                                           
  entry        the model begins producing text
  carriers     the TRAIL at the head · the agent’s mark one space past it
  actions      ⌃C stops the turn and KEEPS the partial text
  esc          nothing — it is not a temporary state
  motion off   no trail, no bloom. The elapsed counter carries liveness
  1-bit        the trail is a BOLD band; the head band is SGR 7
  residue      settled text, no cursor. Nothing replaces the bloom
 
 FOCUS                                                                       
  entry        ⇧⇥ from the prompt, ↑↓, a click, or restored from memory
  carriers     the shape’s own treatment · the ▸ mark · the footer’s key row
  actions      ↑↓ move · ←→ within a row · ⏎ enter or activate
  esc          out one rung
  motion off   unchanged — focus never animated
  1-bit        INVERSE, and the ▸ carries the rest
  residue      REMEMBERED by id. Inactive focus is the wash, not the paint
 
 A WATCH                                                                     
  entry        a long-running job you started, or /watch
  carriers     the footer row · a bar · the entry it points AT
  actions      ←→ along the row · ⏎ scrolls to its entry and opens it
  esc          nothing — the footer is not a scope
  motion off   the bar stops shimmering; the percentage stays
  1-bit        the bar is ## against ..; the name carries identity
  residue      it DROPS ITSELF, and the completion earns a notification
 
 A NOTIFICATION                                                              
  entry        a blocked question · a turn over ~30s · a watched run ending
  carriers     the bell · OSC 9 · the title — three rungs, all opt-in
  actions      none. It is not on screen
  esc          not applicable
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        unchanged
  residue      the new-messages button, if you were scrolled away
 
★ two cells that were BLANK until this table existed
 
  a streaming reply’s MOTION OFF form. The trail and the bloom are
  both motion, and with both gone nothing said the reply was still
  arriving. The elapsed counter had to be promoted to carry it. Every live
  thing retains a non-motion liveness carrier; indeterminate or streaming
  work uses elapsed time.
 
  a watch’s RESIDUE. It drops itself, so being away meant it vanished
  with no trace. That is what put watched-run completion on the
  notification ladder.
    

    State tables — six morecurrent · R-TAB-001 · example R-EXA-092
    six more, and the last two are the ones that had no table anywhere
 
 A TABLE                                                                     
  entry        a call or command returned rows
  carriers     a painted header · ▾ on the sorted column · the residue row
  actions      ↑↓ rows · ⇥ to a header, ⏎ sorts · ⌃⇧C copies VALUES
  esc          out to the transcript, remembering the row
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        the header is inverse; ▾ survives; the focused row inverts
  residue      the window, its count, AND its sort — the order is not the
               document’s, so the residue says so
 
 A PATCH                                                                     
  entry        the model edited a file
  carriers     the path rule · a COLOURED stat · −/+ markers · the gutter
  actions      ⏎ enters · ⌃⇧C copies a UNIFIED DIFF, not the painted rows
  esc          out to the transcript
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        the markers alone. Grounds gone, gutter tone gone, text plain
  residue      the hunks and the stat. ↺ revert while the turn is recent
 
 A PLOT                                                                      
  entry        a command or a tool produced a series
  carriers     the figure · its AXES · a legend · a readout when cursored
  actions      ⏎ enters · ←→ crosshair or camera · 1–9 toggle a series · hover
               moves the readout and NEVER the focus
  esc          out; the camera and the cursor keep their positions
  motion off   a live plot stops repainting on tick; it still patches on data
  1-bit        braille survives; the series are told apart by the legend’s
               marks, never by colour
  residue      the figure, the final camera, the cursor where you left it
 
 AN ATTACHED PTY — the CHILD captures ownership over a block                 
  entry        ⏎ on a terminal block, deliberately
  carriers     the border goes heavy · the head says !! attached · the footer
               names the child and the reserved host escape
  actions      keys go to the child, including ⌃C and esc, except host.detach
  esc          goes to the CHILD. ⌃] is the base-terminal host escape;
               ⌥esc also detaches when the protocol distinguishes it
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        the heavy border is the carrier; the !! survives
  residue      the block, scrollable, no longer captured
 
 A SUBAGENT TAB                                                              
  entry        the model fans out
  carriers     a painted name chip · its hue on all four rules · the footer row
  actions      ⌃⇥ switches · ⌘1–9 jumps · its prompt is LIVE
  esc          its own three scopes. esc never leaves the tab — ⌃⇥ does
  motion off   its walk stops; its elapsed count carries liveness
  1-bit        the NAME carries identity; the hue is gone
  residue      its transcript stays. The parent records what came back
 
 A PASTE CHIP                                                                
  entry        a paste longer than a few lines, or an @ mention
  carriers     the chip · its size BEFORE you attach · a warn past a threshold
  actions      ⏎ opens it to edit · ⌥⌫ drops it · it travels with the message
  esc          closes the edit view, keeping the chip
  motion off   unchanged
  1-bit        the brackets carry it: [#1 json · 47L]
  residue      part of the sent message, and the transcript shows the chip
 
★ three more blank cells, and each was a real hole
 
  A TABLE’S RESIDUE had to say its SORT. The rows are not in the
  document’s order once you sort them, and a reader who scrolled past
  the header has no way to know.
 
  A PLOT’S 1-BIT form could not use colour to separate series, and
  nothing said what did. The LEGEND’S MARKS do — which means a plot
  with more series than marks is a plot that cannot degrade, and that
  is a real limit the plot arm should enforce.
 
  AN ATTACHED PTY’S ESC belongs to the CHILD. It alone sends esc outside
  Calcium; other captured owners handle it on the host, while passive rows
  may declare no-op or not-applicable. The PTY therefore needs its own
  chord and the footer has to say it. Without the table, that cell was
  simply never asked.
    

    Three major rules it broke in its own examplescurrent · R-GLY-001 R-MOT-002 R-EVT-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-093
    three major rules this document broke in its own examples, measured
 
1 · THE MARK SET WAS NEVER WIDTH-CHECKED
  the spinner rules ban East Asian AMBIGUOUS glyphs and say the check
  runs on a SET, not a glyph. The mark vocabulary was never measured:
  
  ●  U+25CF   Ambiguous      ⎿  U+23BF   Narrow
  ▲  U+25B2   Ambiguous      ⟩  U+27E9   Narrow
  ○  U+25CB   Ambiguous      ❯  U+276F   Narrow
  ⋯  U+22EF   Ambiguous      ▸  U+25B8   Narrow
  ▾  U+25BE   Narrow         ✓  U+2713   Narrow
  ✗  U+2717   Narrow         ›  U+203A   Narrow
  
  FOUR AMBIGUOUS, EIGHT NARROW — a mixed set, which is exactly the
  condition that sent the scrollbar to its ascii rung. At
  ambiguousWidth: wide the gutter is two cells for some marks and one
  for others, and every measured height is wrong.
  
  so the mark set takes an ascii rung too, whole:
  ● ⎿ ⟩ ▲ ❯ ▸ ▾ ○ ✓ ✗ › ⋯   →   o `- ? ^ $ > v @ + x * ...
 
2 · THE 800–1600 ms BAND WAS WRONG, NOT THE TABLE
  measured against the catalogue: 8 of 21 sets passed. noise is 300ms,
  triangle 480, bloom 1680, hex 1760. The rule was unshippable.
  
  the property that actually decides whether a thing reads as alive is
  the INTERVAL: every shipped WORK set is 80–200ms; deliberate WAIT sets may
  be slower. Cycle length decides
  VARIETY instead — 4-frame sets repeat every 0.48–0.8s, while a 42-frame
  one does not repeat for five seconds.
 
3 · ORBIT'S 16 ms ARR AGAINST THE 100 ms WINDOW
  key repeat claims 60fps for a camera. But a camera change is a
  DOCUMENT change and a document change takes the window — so the
  stated rate was about six times the real one.
  
  the fix is the exemption's own test: the split is CAUSATION. A held
  arrow is a keypress and the reader is watching for it at 16ms, so
  ORBIT JOINS THE DRAW-NOW SET — alongside echo and focus.
  
  draws now   a keystroke that changes the prompt
              a keystroke that moves focus
              a keystroke that drives a CAMERA or a SLIDER
  the window  a stream patch, a tick, an arriving entry
 
and four smaller ones, fixed rather than argued
 
  the running dot   ONE position: white, still, spinner beside it.
                    Four sections disagreed
  bottom            ⌘↓ everywhere. ⌃↓ is gone
  copy mode         ⌥⇧C. It was sharing ⌃⇧C with copy, and a
                    terminal cannot tell the case apart
  the app's name    calcium, in the header, the label and the path
 
★ and the hue order was assigned SPECTRALLY, which is a CVD hazard
 
  agents 1–5 were red, orange, yellow, lime, green — five identities a
  deuteranope cannot separate. The order is now by PERCEPTUAL
  SEPARATION, and the name carries the rest exactly as the 1-bit
  argument already says it must:
  
   blue   orange   cyan   pink   lime   violet   yellow   green   red   purple 
  
  the first four are separable under every common deficiency, which
  is where a session with three subagents lands.
    

    Three tiers — content, representation, decorationcurrent · R-DEG-001 R-DEG-002 R-COR-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-094
    THREE TIERS, not two — and each degrades its own way
 
  CONTENT       shrinks to its FLOOR; representation substitution happens before
                any final container clip or scroll
                a plot, a table, a mosaic cell, a chip
                visible and recoverable
  
  REPRESENTATIONsubstitutes a smaller FORM saying the same thing
                a sidebar → a rail, a footer → its primary action
  
  DECORATION    truncates with NO MARK, then drops with no trace
                a rule, a spacer, a trailing dash, a box corner
 
★ TRUNCATION MARKS LOSS. A shorter rule has lost nothing.
 
  which is why decoration gets no ellipsis — and why its minimum is a
  THRESHOLD rather than a floor:
  
  content's min      a FLOOR — it WIDENS its container to keep it
  decoration's min   a THRESHOLD — it NEVER widens anything, and
                     below it the decoration simply goes
 
   7/10 ────────────────────────────── 39k/50k █████████░░░   56
   7/10 ────────── 39k/50k █████████░░░   40
   7/10       39k/50k █████████░░░      30
   7/10    39                                  22
 
  the rule fills, then silently goes — and the CONTENT keeps every cell
  it had. A cell that vanishes silently is a bug; a divider that vanishes
  silently is the design.
 
★ SHED, DON’T SHRED — and four kinds get this wrong today (C09 I81)
 
  truncation is for ONE RUN too long for its box. Shedding is for a ROW
  OF PEERS too many for the width. Four kinds apply truncation to a
  shedding problem, which is why every column gives at the same moment.
  
  today   basel… a      b      Δ     ✓   every part, together
  should  a b Δ ✓ +1               one at a time, in a declared order
          a b ✓ +2
          a b +3                     RANK 0 NEVER SHEDS
  
  comparison  the two VALUES never shed — without them it is not a
              comparison
  keyValue    the KEY never sheds — a value with no key is not a fact
  events      the TIME and the mark never shed
  steps       the CURRENT step never sheds
 
  and the last is the agent switcher’s own rule arriving at a fourth
  kind: a row that cannot show you where you are is worse than no row.
    

    A tape, where a row of peers would shedcurrent · R-HON-003 R-STR-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-095
    A ROW OF PEERS SHEDS MEMBERS. A LIST YOU NAVIGATE SLIDES A WINDOW.
 
shedding loses the hidden ones. A TAPE keeps them all and moves the
window to hold the current — like a browser’s tab strip.
 
  ⋯ › main    seams  2:53 ✓   arm  3:46 ✓   count   4:02    ⌃⇥
  ⋯   main    seams  ✓   arm  ✓  › count    2»      ⌃⇥
  ⋯   main   «2  count   › probe  ✓  1»     ⌃⇥
 
  «2 and 1» say how many are off each end — NOTHING IS LOST, only
  offscreen. And the window moves ONLY when the current leaves it,
  which is what makes it read as a tape rather than a cursor dragging
  the row along.
 
two rules make the shedding honest
 
  1  an ALL-OR-NOTHING group goes before any single member. Every
     elapsed TIME goes before one agent does, because knowing an agent
     EXISTS beats knowing how long it has run. Without this the ladder
     is not monotonic — it drops a whole agent to keep a clock.
  
  2  the window moves by the MINIMUM that brings the current back into
     view — the same sentence as FOCUS PULLS THE VIEWPORT, BY THE
     MINIMUM, one axis over.
 
  ★ and moving the window COSTS a «n, which SHRINKS it — so one move
  can push the current straight back out. It settles to a fixed point.
    

    A status has three parts, and a frame is separatecurrent · R-PRI-001 R-COR-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-096
    A STATUS HAS THREE PARTS, and each degrades its own way
 
  the BANNER   decoration either side of a label that NEVER truncates
  the MESSAGE  prose — it WRAPS, because losing the end loses the fact
  the DETAIL   code — it TRUNCATES, and it is BOUNDED with a residue
               row, so it never costs more than a few rows
 
★ and a STATUS is content. A FRAME is the container’s. They COMPOSE.
 
  the same status, three containers, and neither knows about the other
 
  ┌ val loss ──────────────────────────────────── ┐
  │ ────────────── ERROR ────────────── │
  │ ✗ plot failed to render                        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘   framed — a plot HAS a border
  
  ● read_image(loss-curve.png) · failed
    ⎿ ────────── ERROR ──────────
      ✗ decode failed: truncated PNG    the GUTTER is the
                                        containment
  
  ────────────── ERROR ──────────────
  ✗ context exhausted at 50,000 tokens
   retrying in 8s · attempt 2       bare — the prompt rules
                                        are the containment
 
  one status() function, three containers, nine combinations. Baking
  the frame into the error needed a second function for every
  unframed case, which is how a duplicate gets written.
 
and EMPTY is not an error, so the layout says so
 
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐      no banner, no ▲, no red
  │           No data.            │      centred on BOTH axes — the
  └──────────────────────────────┘      one place that is right,
                                         because a block with nothing
                                         in it has slack on both
    

    A transient panel floats, between two rulescurrent · R-QST-001 R-OWN-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-097
    A TRANSIENT PANEL FLOATS, BETWEEN TWO RULES
 
the completion menu, find, a chip preview: these are MENUS, and a menu
draws OVER what is behind it. NOTHING ABOVE MOVES.
 
  ● The parser handles quotes with a single boolean, so a nested
    quote flips it back instead of counting a level.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   › /colour  tint the chrome for this project 
     /compact  summarise the conversation so far 
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ❯ /colour▌
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 
  the prompt already has a rule BELOW it, so the panel sitting BETWEEN
  TWO RULES is what says it is a panel and not a reply. Without that
  boundary it reads as transcript content, which is the one thing it
  is not.
 
★ and it never REFLOWS the transcript — a keystroke costs a few rows,
not a whole re-solve.
 
three shapes, three names, one layer order
 
  a PANEL    floats above the prompt, between two rules. DISMISSABLE:
             a click off it CLOSES it, and the click stops there
  a PEEK     anchored BESIDE an element, and it takes NO KEYS — it
             is a projection of focus, so focus leaving closes it
  an OVERLAY modal, and it OWNS input. NOT dismissable: clicking
             off it does nothing, because an owner is waiting
  
  overlay › panel › peek › base   — and this is the SCROLL
  priority too, so one ordering does both jobs.
 
★ the WHEEL goes to the innermost scrollable under the POINTER, highest
layer first. The ARROWS go to the one you are INSIDE.
 
  the pointer says where it is; the keyboard does not. That asymmetry
  is the whole rule — asking a wheel to click first is asking twice.
 
and a TEXT preview scrolls where an IMAGE resizes
 
  that is the axis, NOT how big the thing is. An image has a cell
  rectangle the producer declares and the engine fills, so it is whole
  at every width — a cropped preview shows the wrong thing and reads as
  a bug. Text cannot resize, so it gets a bounded window and the same
  scrollbar column everything else uses.
  
  which leaves ⏎ for EDITING rather than for merely seeing.
    

    Input ownership — what was in flightcurrent · R-OWN-002 R-QST-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-098
    THE LADDER SAYS WHO OWNS THE KEYBOARD NOW. It says nothing about an
event already IN FLIGHT when ownership changed — and that is where the
harm is.
 
you are typing. A child raises a choice-only question and holds the prompt. Your ⏎
arrives. Turning an intended SUBMIT into a permission DENIAL is wrong,
even when the safe choice is the one initially focused.
 
★ EVENTS ASSIGNED TO ONE OWNER MUST NOT BE REPLAYED AGAINST ANOTHER.
  A newly presented question requires a FRESH, DELIBERATE activation.
  EVERY OWNER TRANSITION INCREMENTS AN OWNERSHIP GENERATION.
 
  presses, repeats, releases and pending activations retain the generation
  where they began. A later owner can never receive them.
 
  with key-release reporting, wait for the held key to lift. WITHOUT it the
  question enters ACTIVATION-GUARDED state: the first ambiguous keyboard
  activation before a neutral/key-up boundary is refused, naming why. A fresh
  pointer press belongs to the new owner epoch and keeps ordinary one-click semantics.
 
four moments, and the draft survives all of them
 
  ❯ refactor the parser to handle nested quotes▌
  
  ⟩  seams  may I write to package.json?
  approve    › deny    reply…                                                 
  the draft is HELD — buffer, caret, chips and undo
  
  ▲ ⏎ refused · this question arrived after you pressed.
    Press again to answer.
  
  ❯ refactor the parser to handle nested quotes▌
    answered · and the draft came back exactly as it was
 
★ REUSING THE EDITOR IS NOT REUSING ITS STATE
 
  ONE line-editor implementation is right. SAME HISTORY is too broad.
  A normal prompt, a commit-message answer, a paste-chip editor and
  each subagent’s prompt need separate buffers and appropriately
  scoped histories and undo stacks — otherwise a question overwrites a
  half-written instruction, undo crosses between unrelated editors, or
  A SENSITIVE ANSWER APPEARS IN ORDINARY PROMPT HISTORY.
 
★ AN INSPECTION CHOICE IS NOT AN ANSWER
 
  ⟩  seams  may I run rg --stats -uu here?
  › deny    approve once    show full diff    always allow rg --stats -uu here 
  
the third choice is an INSPECTION, not an answer; there is no second key-only path
  
  it SUSPENDS the question, keeps its identity, and esc inside it
  leaves the INSPECTION — not the request. EVERY QUESTION RESOLVES
  EXACTLY ONCE, cancellation and expiry included.
 
  ★ and the grant NAMES WHAT IT GRANTS: the -uu was the entire
    reason for asking, so “always allow rg here” would grant a looser
    thing than the one that was reviewed.
 
and in a SAFETY question, the SAFE choice is initially FOCUSED
 
  an earlier pass drew approval with approve initially focused. If the
  first ambiguous keyboard activation begun before a question arrived were honoured, that
  single cell would be the difference between a denial and a write.
    

    Wrapping, truncation and the atomic chipcurrent · R-TXT-001 R-STR-003 R-STR-004 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-099
    THE PROMPT GROWS AND WRAPS. A CALL TRUNCATES.
 
prose WRAPS because losing the end loses the fact. Code and paths
TRUNCATE because a fragment of a path is still a path you can read.
 
  ❯ refactor the parser so a nested quote counts a level rather
    than flipping a flag, and check the escaping path too▌
  
  the BOX caps against the live viewport and scrolls; the TEXT does not truncate.
 
  ● read_file(src/inte…/ion/parser/parse.ts) · 184 lines
  ● read_file(src/in…/rser/parse.ts) · 184
  ● read_file(sr…/arse.ts)
  
  and a path truncates in the MIDDLE, because the head says where and
  the tail says what. Either end alone is the wrong half.
 
★ A KIND SHORTENS ITSELF, given the width it got
 
  not a set of pre-computed forms that might not fit. The engine hands
  a box its solved width; the kind decides what goes in it. Otherwise a
  path is middle-truncated by its form and then TAIL-truncated again by
  the composer — which is a real defect this pass found:
  
  wrong   src/int…/n/parse…     cut twice, and it shows
  right   src/…/er/parse.ts      cut once, by the kind
 
★ A CHIP IS ATOMIC — it never breaks across a wrap
 
  ❯ look at  parse.ts  and  #1 json · 47L  then
    compare with  construct.ts  before you change it
  
  prose wraps at WORDS, and a chip is one word that happens to be
  painted. A half-painted chip is not a chip with a line break in it —
  it is TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE CHIPS.
 
★ A NUMBER ALIGNS ON ITS POINT, not its edge
 
  inline-start aligned aligned on the point
  val loss   0.0372 val loss     0.0372
  accuracy   0.941  accuracy     0.941
  lr         3e-4   lr        3e-4
  steps      1284   steps     1284
  
  align: r lines up the LAST character, which puts 0.0372 and 3e-4 in
  different places. The column declares where the point sits and every
  cell aligns to it — and AN INTEGER ALIGNS WHERE ITS POINT WOULD BE, so
  1284 ends exactly where 0.941’s point is.
 
★ PROSE IN A CELL WRAPS AT THE CELL WIDTH, and width feeds height
 
  note              cause             fix
  the parser flips  no notion of an   a depth counter
  on every quote    escape at all     plus an escape flag
  
  the one place the pass order could loop, and it does NOT: the cell’s
  width is solved, the text wraps at that width, and the row’s height is
  the tallest cell. HEIGHT NEVER FEEDS BACK INTO WIDTH, so one re-fit is
  a fixed point rather than an iteration.

    Replace or float, and where a chip previewscurrent · R-QST-001 R-STA-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-101
    REPLACE OR FLOAT — does the ANSWER need the prompt?
 
one rule for every popup consumer, and it settles a question the
dismissable axis could not.
 
   consumer        prompt      so it
   an approval     not needed  REPLACES · blocks
   a choice        not needed  REPLACES · blocks
   a typed reply   NEEDED      FLOATS   · blocks
   a peek          NEEDED      FLOATS   · does not block
   completion      NEEDED      FLOATS   · does not block
   find            NEEDED      FLOATS   · does not block
 
  a choice-only question REPLACES the prompt because the prompt has no
  job: there is nothing to type. The moment reply… is chosen the prompt
  HAS one, so the question moves UP and the prompt goes live beneath it.
 
  ⟩  seams  may I write to package.json?
  approve    › deny    reply…                                                 
  ↓ → to reply…
  
  ⟩  seams  may I write to package.json?
  approve    deny    › reply…                                                 
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ❯ it also needs an escape flag▌
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 
  ★ BLOCKING AND REPLACING ARE INDEPENDENT. A typed reply BLOCKS and
  FLOATS, which is the combination that proves it — and it never becomes
  dismissable, because an owner is still waiting. FLOATS is placement, not
  PANEL semantics; this uses overlay ownership at the prompt anchor.

  focus in the TRANSCRIPT   a PEEK, anchored BESIDE the element
  focus in the PROMPT       a MENU PANEL above the prompt,
                            where completion and find already are
  
  a chip is INLINE in a wrapping editor, so anchoring beside it puts the
  preview somewhere different on every keystroke. While composing, every
  transient panel belongs in ONE PLACE.

    View state is not liveness, and a model’s one shapecurrent · R-MOT-007 R-STA-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-102
    “LIVE” WAS CONFLATING TWO ORTHOGONAL THINGS
 
does the CONTENT change? and does it have VIEW STATE? are different
questions — and live named a container for the first while gating the
second. The view changing is a RENDER; the data changing is a PATCH.
 
   kind            view state     content
   a 3D plot       a camera       settled or patched — orbits either way
   a 2D plot       a cursor       settled or patched
   a table         sort + scroll  settled or patched
   a terminal      a scroll offset patched while attached
   an image        a zoom         settled
   a paragraph     none           streamed, then settled
   a patch         none           settled
 
  which leaves two ORDINARY mechanisms and no category: every block can
  be PATCHED, and a block declares whether it has VIEW STATE. Neither
  needs a wrapper, and live as a kind can go.
 
★ A 3D PLOT IS INTERACTIVE BECAUSE IT HAS A CAMERA, not because it is
live. Settled an hour ago, from a call that finished — it STILL ORBITS.
 
  ● plot(attractor) · 0.6s
      1.0┨        ⡇⡇⣿⣿⣿⡇⡇
         ┨   ⣿⣿⡇⡇⡇⡇⡇⡇⡇⡇⣿⣿
    −0.5╂━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
      ←→ orbit   ↑↓ tilt   o auto   r reset   esc out
      az 60°   tilt 10°
 
★ KEYBOARD CONTROLS APPEAR ONLY INSIDE; POINTER READOUT MAY PREVIEW OUTSIDE
 
  at rest   no controls; no readout until the plot has a declared cursor
  hover     pointer preview moves the readout without entering; leaving keeps it
  focused   the way IN — ⏎ enter; a persisted readout may remain
  inside    the full keyboard controls, and the readout follows the cursor
  
  and all of it sits DIRECTLY UNDER THE PLOT — not in chrome elsewhere,
  which is why the controls used to read as belonging to the container
  rather than the figure.
  
  the control row is a REPRESENTATION, so it sheds descriptions and then
  becomes ? keys rather than disappearing at narrow widths.
 
★ HOW A MODEL’S ANSWER IS FORMATTED — and it is ONE SHAPE
 
  ● The parser handles quotes with a single boolean, so a nested
    quote flips it back instead of counting a level.
  
  ● I won’t add a bypass for the approval gate — that is the one
    path the posture exists to hold.
  
  ● I’m not sure this is the right fix. I haven’t checked whether
    the tokeniser re-enters this path after an escape.
  
  an explanation, a refusal and a hedge are the SAME SHAPE, because THE
  SYSTEM CANNOT TELL THEM APART AND MUST NOT PRETEND IT CAN — there is
  no classifier, and colouring an answer by what it seems to mean would
  be a guess wearing the authority of chrome.
  
  the one thing that DOES change the shape is the content’s own
  STRUCTURE: prose wraps, a fenced block does not. The renderer acts on
  structure it can PARSE, never on meaning it would have to INFER.
    

    The ownership ladder — who owns the keyboardcurrent · R-OWN-001 R-OWN-002 R-INT-007 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-103
    THE QUESTION IS NOT WHERE IS FOCUS — IT IS WHO OWNS THE KEYBOARD
 
exactly one thing does, at every moment. §15 listed SCOPES and never
said what a scope competes with, so a question, copy mode, an attached
PTY and a block’s interior were four separate special cases.
 
   owner       raised by            takes                  leaves by
   the CHILD   an attached PTY      all but host.detach ⌃] host escape
   COPY MODE   ⌥⇧V froze the screen every key            esc, or a copy
   a QUESTION  choice or text        declared actions;   resolves exactly once
                                     rejects held scope   by answer · safe exit
   a SUBSTATE  find · completion     its own, then the    esc closes the
               history search        prompt’s            SUBSTATE
   the INSIDE  a camera · a cursor   ←→ ↑↓ and letters   esc leaves it
   the SCOPE   prompt · transcript   everything else      esc out one rung
 
★ EVERY ROUTED ACTION GETS ONE DECISION AT EACH RUNG.
 
  HANDLE             this is the one owner that acts
  REJECT             consume it and explain when silence would look broken
  PASS               continue downward
  GLOBAL-INTERCEPT   take the registry-declared exception
  
  a blocking question handles its answer actions and REJECTS unrelated
  typing; it never passes keys into the held prompt. Esc still resolves
  exactly one temporary owner.
  While it is open, pointer activation may commit only answer or inspection
  targets. Hits on the held scope are consumed without action. Wheel/page
  scroll needs a declared question/inspection viewport or background-scroll policy.
 
global-intercept candidates use an explicit OWNER-APPLICABILITY table
 
  interrupt   CHILD handles; QUESTION and COPY MODE reject; an ordinary
                running owner handles tool/turn interrupt; idle rejects silently
  page-scroll COPY MODE rejects while frozen; otherwise the active viewport
                handles without moving focus
  the wheel   is not delivered in COPY MODE or while mouse tracking is off;
                otherwise its pointer-hit owner handles it
  
  these are declared overrides, not contradictions in the ladder. Apps
  may register one only with an owner, fallback and collision test.
 
★ EVERY OWNER SAYS SO, in the footer’s last line
 
  ⏎ send   ⇧⏎ newline   ⇥ complete   ⇧⇥ transcript
   inside   ←→ orbit   ↑↓ tilt   o auto   r reset   esc out
   find   ↑↓ hits   ⏎ open   esc close   3 of 14
   question   declared actions   esc safe path
   copy   ←→↑↓ extend   ⏎ copy   esc out · the screen is frozen
   attached   keys → child   ⌃] host escape   ⌥esc enhanced detach
  
  AN OWNER YOU CANNOT SEE IS AN OWNER YOU WILL FIGHT. Every rung retains
  owner plus its highest-ranked reachable safe action. Ordinary rungs also
  show primary action, safe exit and help; the complete map is reachable.
 
★ A TAB IS ITS OWN FRAME — its transcript, prompt, scroll AND focus
 
  ⌃⇥ away and back finds it exactly as you left it. That persistence is
  what makes a tab a TAB rather than a view toggle — if switching lost
  your place, esc would want to leave it.
    

    Focus survives a drop, and ←→’s five jobscurrent · R-STA-003 R-INT-004 R-KEY-007 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-104
    FOCUS SURVIVES A DROP — and the +n inherits it
 
a part can VANISH on a resize (§93), and focus memory is by id — so a
shed part’s id renders nothing.
 
  val loss  0.0372  ↓ from 0.41
  ↓ the width goes
  val loss  0.0372  +1
  
  focus falls to the NEAREST SURVIVING part in declaration order — and
  if the +n that replaced it is on screen, FOCUS LANDS THERE. ⏎ expands
  what it stands for, so the shed parts stay REACHABLE rather than gone.
  
  a focus that vanishes is a focus the reader has to go and find again.
 
★ A BLOCK MAY EMIT SEVERAL ELEMENTS ON ONE ROW
 
       1 val loss    2 accuracy    3 gpu util 
  
  a legend is THREE buttons where it was one block; a mosaic is three
  cells. ←→ moves BETWEEN them; ↑↓ leaves the row — and the conformance
  checker’s ordering and disjointness predicates were written when this
  could not happen.
 
★ ←→ HAS FIVE JOBS, and the SCOPE decides which
 
  the prompt          move the caret
  the transcript      nothing — ↑↓ moves, and rows are whole
  a row of elements   move BETWEEN elements on the row
  inside a block      the crosshair, the camera, or a value
  a question          choose
  
  it had three when §18 was written. The rows-of-elements case did not
  exist, and neither did the tape.
 
★ THE CLICK THAT DISMISSES DOES NOT ALSO ACT
 
  the thing you meant to hit was COVERED a moment ago, so a press that
  closed the panel AND activated what was underneath would be acting on
  something you could not see when you decided to press.
  
  ONE GESTURE, ONE EFFECT — which is the same shape as esc pops one
  rung, on the pointer instead of the keyboard.
 
★ and one REFUSAL, stated rather than left out
 
  NOTHING MOVES THE TAPE’S WINDOW WITHOUT MOVING THE CURRENT. There is
  no scroll-the-switcher key and there should not be: the window exists
  to keep the current visible, so a key that moved one without the other
  would make the › and the window disagree.
  
  an omission reads as an oversight; a refusal reads as a decision.
    

    Five primitives the harness never neededcurrent · R-PRI-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-105
    FIVE PRIMITIVES THE HARNESS NEVER NEEDED
 
a general app wants these and the agent surface does not, so they were
missing rather than refused. Each is built from what already exists.
 
a TREE — the twisty is CONTENT, the guides are DECORATION
 
  ▾ src
  │  ▾ interaction
  │  │  ▸ parser
  │  │    frame.ts                      4.1 kB
  │  ▸ data
    package.json                        1.2 kB
  
  so at narrow widths the GUIDES go first and the names never do — and
  depth is capped by §93’s floor rule, not by a constant.
 
a FORM — the label is Fixed, the field Grows, the hint is decoration
 
   name        prism-serve
   port        80▌
               ✗ ports below 1024 need root
   replicas    3
               0 stops the service
  
  › save    cancel                                                            
  an ERROR REPLACES THE HINT rather than joining it — two lines under
  one field is two things competing to be read. And it uses the same ✗
  and the same tone as every other failure, so a form error is not a new
  visual idea.
 
a SPLIT — the divider is a CONTROL
 
  src/              │ export function layout(b, w, h) {
    interaction/    │   b = chooseRep(b, w);
    data/           ┃   solveW(b, w);
  README.md         │   return b;
  
  drag it, or ⌥←→ from either side — the SCROLLBAR’s rule on the other
  axis. The focused pane takes the accent ON the divider, so which side
  owns the arrows is visible without a label.
 
a COMMAND PALETTE — and it is a PANEL whose list is a LADDER
 
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ❯ open▌        3 of 61
   › open file         ⌘O
     toggle sidebar    ⌃B

     +58 more
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  nothing new: a PANEL (§96), a LADDER, and a RESIDUE. The framework

a TOAST — and the rule that keeps it honest
 
   ✓ saved to disk  3s 
  
  transient, and it takes NO KEYS. ★ WHAT A TOAST ANNOUNCES IS ALSO IN
  THE RECORD — a toast is a courtesy, never the only place something was

  §11 already refused a FLOATING toast and was right: this one lives

    Where two rules meet — six composition casescurrent · R-STA-002 R-OWN-001 R-QST-002 R-COR-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-106
    WHERE TWO RULES MEET — the cases neither rule answers alone
 
individual rules are well specified. The document is thin exactly where
two of them meet, and that is where interaction models break.
 
1 · A QUESTION ARRIVES WHILE A PANEL IS OPEN
 
  a panel is DISMISSABLE and a question is NOT. Two layers, and one of
  them is about to take the keyboard.
  
  THE PANEL CLOSES FIRST, and its state is held with the prompt’s.
  A panel is a thing you opened; a question is a thing that arrived. The
  arriving one cannot silently sit under something you were reading, and
  stacking two dismissable-versus-not layers makes esc ambiguous.
  
  and the question still takes the activation guard described in INPUT
  OWNERSHIP — so the ⏎ that would have taken a completion does not answer it.
 
2 · A RESIZE WHILE INSIDE A PLOT, WITH A MODAL PENDING
 
  three rules want the same moment: a resize keeps your SCOPE (§59), a
  modal OWNS input (§102), and focus falls forward by id (§103).
  
  THE LADDER DECIDES, because it always does. The modal owns the
  keyboard, so the resize changes what is DRAWN and not who OWNS it — the
  plot re-solves underneath, the camera is kept, and when the question
  resolves you are back inside the plot exactly where you were.
  
  ★ a resize is a RENDER event. It can never change the OWNER — which is
  the same reason §59 says it cannot change the scope.
 
3 · TWO QUESTIONS, AND THE FIRST IS BEING INSPECTED
 
  §97 says an inspection SUSPENDS a question. The queue rule says a second
  question WAITS. What does the second one do while the first is
  suspended and therefore not on screen?
  
  IT WAITS, and the inspection is not a resolution. The queue is of
  UNRESOLVED questions, and suspended is unresolved — which is the
  whole point of the word. Leaving the inspection returns to the first
  question, not to the second.
  
  EVERY QUESTION RESOLVES EXACTLY ONCE, and a suspension is not one.
 
4 · A WATCHED RUN FINISHES WHILE ITS ENTRY IS EVICTED
 
  the visible window evicts at a cap. A watch retains a stable EVENT ID
  in the durable record, so it can outlive that event's current rendering.
  
  ⏎ REHYDRATES THE WATCHED EVENT, preserving its identity.
  Completion is a new durable event linked to that watched ID, so it
  appears at the end without pretending to replace history. The watch
  can open either fact; eviction changed only the window.
 
5 · THE CONNECTION DROPS WHILE A QUESTION IS OPEN
 
  the child that asked is gone. The question is still on screen and
  still owns the keyboard.
  
  IT RESOLVES ITSELF, VISIBLY — as EXPIRED, not as denied.
  
  ○ the question expired ·  seams  disconnected after 41s
  
  denied would be a lie about what happened, and leaving it open would
  hold the keyboard for an owner that no longer exists. Expiry is the
  third resolution, and it is why §97 says CANCELLATION AND EXPIRY
  INCLUDED rather than just answered.
 
6 · A SORTED TABLE REORDERS UNDER A HELD POINTER
 
  a live table patches while you are pressing on a row. The row at
  those coordinates on RELEASE is a different row.
  
  THE GESTURE IS BOUND TO THE ELEMENT’S IDENTITY, not the coordinates.
  Press ARMS the element it landed on; release COMMITS only if the
  pointer is still over THAT ELEMENT. Otherwise nothing happens, and
  nothing happening is correct — it is the pointer’s version of §97’s
  rule about events assigned to one owner.
 
★ the thread through all six
 
  EVERY ONE IS ANSWERED BY A RULE THAT ALREADY EXISTS, applied to a
  case it was not written for. None of them needed a new mechanism —
  which is the test for whether the rules are the right ones.
  
  and the one thing they share: A RESIZE, A PATCH AND AN ORDINARY CONTENT
  ARRIVAL ARE RENDER EVENTS. They change what is drawn; they never change
  the owner. An ownership-request event declares that change explicitly.
    

    The semantic tree, linear rendering and terminal boundarycurrent · R-ACC-001 R-TRU-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-107
    THE CELL GRID IS A PROJECTION. IT IS NOT THE INTERFACE.
 
everything drawn also exists as a semantic node
 
  id          the same stable id used by focus, patches and pointer arms
  role        entry · question · button · link · table · row · figure…
  name        what it is, without colour, position or punctuation
  description context needed to understand it, without repeating the name
  value       source value plus a human valueText, not the painted string
  state       focused · selected · expanded · busy · stale · invalid…
  position    3 of 18, when membership has an order
  actions     the same action ids the keymap resolves
  relations   owns · describes · labelled-by, when needed
 
a repaint changes CELLS, not identity. A resize changes representation,
not the name. A patch never arbitrarily moves focus; if it removes the focused
node, focus re-resolves by the declared stable-id fallback.
 
the semantic tree has two renderings
 
  rich      the cursor-addressed interface in this document
  linear    an append-only stream of semantic events
 
linear is selectable before the first frame through --linear, the
CALCIUM_RENDER_MODE=linear environment setting, or persistent config.
accessibility.screenReader=auto chooses linear when no rich semantic bridge
is available. The chosen route appears in /capabilities.
 
linear mode uses no alternate screen, mouse tracking, cursor-addressed repaint
or animation. It never rewrites emitted semantic events; only the active input
line edits in place. Choice questions emit a numbered question event and later
a resolution event: replace/float is rich placement, never history mutation.
Choice questions use numbered choices;
text questions use a labelled line editor; mixed forms add an explicit text arm.
A running call announces start, useful elapsed milestones, blockage and
completion — not spinner frames. Streaming prose arrives in coherent batches.
 
ANNOUNCEMENTS COME FROM SEMANTIC EVENTS, NEVER FROM DIFFING THE SCREEN.
announce is none / polite / assertive, with deduplication and rate limits.
A repaint of the same fact does not say it twice.
Their transport is declared: linear stdout or a named local semantic bridge.
If no rich-mode bridge exists, auto falls back to linear; it never claims that
an internal tree alone is exposed to a terminal screen reader.
 
a figure owes accessibleName, summary, a data view and, when the summary
cannot be safe, a long description. Nothing important is hover-only.
An image without authored alternative text says so and offers metadata and
a description action; braille art is a rendering, not an alternative.
 
ONLY THE RENDERER WRITES TERMINAL CONTROL SEQUENCES.
 
model text, tool output, filenames, branches, URLs, logs and errors are
UNTRUSTED TEXT — even when they came from this machine.
 
  C0 / C1 controls   shown as visible escapes
  ESC / CSI / OSC    parsed, never replayed
  ANSI colour         allowlisted into semantic spans
  OSC 8 links         rebuilt from a validated destination
  bidi controls       isolated or shown; never reorder neighbours
  BEL · title · OSC 52only through named notify, title and copy actions
 
a payload cannot forge chrome, close a panel, create a question, change the
title, write the clipboard or ring the bell. Attached PTY emulation is the
bounded exception: display controls stay inside its rectangle and host-scoped
effects do not escape it.
 
conformance fixtures include hostile filenames, forged hyperlinks, OSC 52,
bidi text and ANSI-shaped logs. “Copy source” escapes control bytes; an
explicit COPY RAW action may exist only with an unsafe-data warning.
    

    Capability vectors resolve actionscurrent · R-CAP-001 R-KEY-007 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-108
    A TERMINAL IS NOT CAPABLE OR INCAPABLE. IT HAS A VECTOR.
 
  keyboard   legacy · modified keys · press/repeat · release
  colour     1 · 4 · 8 · 24 bit
  glyphs     ascii · unicode · ambiguous width · emoji width
  pointer    none · buttons · motion · wheel
  surface    cursor-addressed · linear
  motion     full · reduced · off
  links      OSC 8 · text destination
  clipboard  OSC 52 · ordinary copy
  notify     OSC 9 / 777 · bell · none
  title      OSC 2 · unchanged
  output     ordinary · synchronised
 
each field carries a value and provenance: detected, configured, inherited
or fallback. /capabilities records the vector, its evidence and every
fallback it caused. A remote hop or multiplexer may change fields independently.
 
BINDINGS BEGIN WITH ACTIONS, NOT CHORDS.
 
  action      focus.next
  candidates  ⇥ · platform alternative · /focus-next
  owner       the scope allowed to handle it
  repeat      none · OS · DAS/ARR pair
 
resolution is deterministic
  1  take a valid reader override
  2  remove chords owned by the OS or terminal
  3  remove chords the protocol cannot distinguish
  4  remove collisions inside one owner
  5  choose the first remaining platform candidate
  6  keep the named command for non-capture actions; keep a base-terminal
     host-escape chord for captured owners
 
A CAPABILITY MAKES AN ACTION BETTER, NEVER POSSIBLE.
Shift+Enter, modified arrows, clipboard chords and direct watch jumps are
enhancements. /doctor keys verifies what reaches the app. The footer shows
the chord that works in this session, not a preferred chord that does not.
 
a captured child reserves one host.detach action because a /command cannot
reach the host while capture is active. Its base candidate is ⌃]; ⌥esc is an
enhancement. Resolution collision-tests and may rebind the base candidate,
but may never leave capture without a visible, reachable host escape.
 
re-resolution is a render event. It records changed bindings; it never moves
focus, changes a value, replays input or takes the keyboard from its owner.
    

    Responsive space and international textcurrent · R-TXT-001 R-CAP-001 R-STR-003 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-109
    WIDTH AND HEIGHT ARE BOTH CAPABILITIES. LANGUAGE IS NOT A WIDTH ASSUMPTION.
 
  WIDTH  comfortable   80+ columns
         compact       40–79 columns; lower-priority chrome sheds
         narrow        20–39 columns; tables linearize; choices stack
         postage-stamp under 20 columns; one safe action at a time
  
  HEIGHT comfortable   16+ rows
         compact       8–15 rows; body keeps owner and safe action
         postage-stamp under 8 rows; one safe action at a time
 
width and height each propose a rung; the MORE CONSTRAINED rung wins. Prompt growth is
capped against the live viewport, never a fixed ten rows. No rung may clip a
permission choice, failure reason, current owner or focused identity.
 
text operations name their coordinate system and locale contract
 
  caret / delete      extended grapheme clusters
  word movement       locale-aware boundaries, including languages without spaces
  wrapping            locale-aware line breaking, not whitespace alone
  bidi                logical inline-start/end; isolate code, paths, URLs and ids
  IME                 composition is one edit; commands do not fire while composing
  search / sort       declared case folding, collation and normalization
  numbers / dates     locale grouping, decimal separator, plural and duration
 
emoji ZWJ sequences, variation selectors, flags, skin tones and combining marks
remain one grapheme for ordinary editing. Labels measure intrinsically; mandatory
choices wrap or stack rather than truncate. Direction of reading is never assumed.
    

    Three records, a state product and the extension doorcurrent · R-COR-001 R-STA-001 · retained example blocks generated from registry · example R-EXA-110
    THE EVENT RECORD, VISIBLE WINDOW AND MODEL CONTEXT ARE THREE THINGS.
 
  EVENT RECORD    durable semantic facts in order
  VISIBLE WINDOW  the current projection of those facts
  MODEL CONTEXT   the compiled input for the next turn
 
the record stores stable id, sequence, source, parent, content reference and
state transitions — never cursor-addressed frames. Streaming writes start,
patch and settle events, not forty nearly identical pictures.
 
the visible window may fold, filter, bound, shed or evict. EVERY CONTENT OR
EVENT OMISSION LEAVES A RESIDUE with range, count, reason and retrieval action.
Pure decoration is not an event and may shed without residue. Rehydrating
old rows changes the window and nothing else.
 
model context may include an event, exclude it, or replace a range with a
summary. Each item points to event ids; a summary names and can open its range.
COMPACTION CHANGES CONTEXT, NOT THE RECORD.
SCROLLBACK EVICTION CHANGES THE WINDOW, NOT CONTEXT.
RESIZE CHANGES REPRESENTATION, NOT EITHER HISTORY.
 
state is a product; a component declares only the axes it uses
 
  lifecycle     pending · live · blocked · settled
  outcome       none · succeeded · failed · cancelled
  resolution    open · answered · cancelled · expired
  ownership     none · available · active · captured
  focus         absent · remembered · focused
  pointer       away · hover · armed · dragging
  selection     none · selected · mixed
  choice        unchosen · chosen
  disclosure    leaf · collapsed · expanded
  availability  enabled · readonly · disabled
  freshness     fresh · stale · unknown
  validity      unchecked · valid · invalid
 
FOCUSED IS NOT SELECTED OR CHOSEN. HOVER DOES NOT ACTIVATE.
RUNNING IS NOT FRESH. REMEMBERED FOCUS DOES NOT OWN THE KEYBOARD.
 
every component keeps the seven-fact component table in §§90–91 and also declares
semantics, announcement, state axes and composition. An extension adds:
 
  type / version      stable namespaced identity
  consumer            the real surface that needs it
  ownership           actions handled, rejected, passed or intercepted
  copy                source form and named alternatives
  responsive ladder   width and height rungs, identity preserved
  capabilities        enhancement, fallback and linear form
  trust boundary      untrusted fields and parser
  registries          tokens, glyphs, actions and bindings added
  conformance         themes · 1-bit · ASCII · motion off · linear ·
                      narrow · short · locale · hostile content
 
registration is additive and collision-checked. A new token has a semantic
name; a glyph has width and ASCII rung; an action has owner and base-terminal
route, plus a command fallback unless capture forbids it; a state has composition
cases. Experimental components may exist
without a consumer, but enter core only after one real surface exercises them.
 
THE EXTENSION DOOR IS WIDE OPEN, BUT SHAPED.
    

    The rules, condensedcurrent · R-SPC-001 · example R-EXA-111
    Generated from CURRENT registry records only. This is a projection, never a paraphrased second source.
 
STRUCTURE
  Keep one durable event record, one rendered window, and one model context. Eviction changes the window; compaction changes context; neither erases history.  [R-COR-001]
  A call has one head and one gutter, with at most one bounded body when output exists.  [R-STR-001]
  At transcript level, one blank row separates sibling entries; spacing inside a body belongs to that block.  [R-STR-002]
  Every nested level costs three columns, and nesting is limited by width while the deepest child still clears its own minimum width.  [R-STR-003]
  Content stops one column before the inline-end edge.  [R-STR-004]
 
COLOUR
  Framework status red means failure and override red means unsafe override; red is never the only carrier. Syntax, removal, and identity retain their declared roles.  [R-COL-001]
  The tone budget is regional: an entry has three tones, while code, plots, and patches carry their own adjacent palettes.  [R-COL-002]
  A ground is for an extent; a tone is for a mark. Things take a ground and facts about things take a tone.  [R-COL-003]
  An actionable, status, or interaction ground is never the only carrier; dense data owes a readout.  [R-COL-004]
  Focus intensifies by shape: an unpainted run or box inverts, a frame takes its border or axes, a control washes, and a painted identity chip bolds and marks.  [R-COL-005]
 
MOTION
  A specimen animation may change only the glyph in a cell or that cell’s colour, opacity, or brightness. Transform, translate, scale, rotate, and layout motion are forbidden. Per-character stagger is retained. Glyph-swap frames resolve through a one-cell capability rung; ambiguous Unicode falls back to registered one-cell ASCII frames.  [R-MOT-005]
  Motion says that state is changing or something is live. Semantic animation says what is happening, never merely look here.  [R-MOT-006]
  A call’s shape does not depend on its duration.  [R-MOT-007]
  The bloom family belongs to the agent and nothing else uses it.  [R-MOT-008]
 
INTERACTION
  Interaction uses visible scopes, not hidden modes.  [R-INT-001]
  No single-key command exists in any scope where typing is possible.  [R-INT-002]
  Scrolling is not a scope and never moves focus.  [R-INT-003]
  Focus pulls the viewport by the minimum displacement required to reveal it.  [R-INT-004]
  An inside-bearing continuous control cannot commit its domain value from outside; declared readouts may preview and direct-action controls have no inside state.  [R-INT-005]
  Every consumed state-changing pointer gesture lands on a state a key can reach.  [R-INT-006]
  Escape takes the current host owner’s declared safe path at most one rung; in an attached PTY it belongs to the child.  [R-INT-007]
  Nothing moves the reader without asking. Rejected commands explain; passive untargeted pointer events may remain silent.  [R-INT-008]
 
HONESTY
  A dash is not a zero.  [R-HON-001]
  A stale reading says when it was taken.  [R-HON-002]
  A bounded window says what it dropped.  [R-HON-003]
  A refusal states its reason and is never red.  [R-HON-004]
  A number carries its unit.  [R-HON-005]
  Copy takes the source, never the rendering.  [R-HON-006]
  The event record, visible window, and model context never masquerade as one.  [R-HON-007]
 
DEGRADATION
  Every actionable, status, and interaction distinction has two independent carriers and survives without colour. Dense data may shed colour-only detail only when a named readout preserves the meaning.  [R-COR-003]
  Every semantic glyph declares a collision-free ASCII fallback, width by capability, and reservedCells equal to its widest representation. The renderer pads the selected representation to that reservation.  [R-GLY-001]
  Capabilities form a vector, not a ladder. Every action has a base-terminal route; enhanced protocols improve bindings but never create the only route.  [R-CAP-001]
  Every component exposes semantics and announcement policy. Linear semantic events are append-only and non-animated; only the active input editor mutates in place.  [R-ACC-001]
  Only the renderer emits terminal controls. User, model, tool, path, URL, and log content is escaped; a PTY interprets controls only inside its emulator boundary.  [R-TRU-001]
  Every distinction survives to one-bit rendering.  [R-DEG-001]
  A capability makes things better, never possible.  [R-DEG-002]
  Width is checked on a simultaneously rendered set, not on an isolated glyph.  [R-DEG-003]
